methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Drones & Autonomous (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 5 same-sector peers exist in Drones & Autonomous, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Terra Drone operates in the Drones & Autonomous sector and completed an IPO on the Tokyo exchange. The valuation exercise faces material constraints: while six private companies operate in this space, the peer set lacks sufficient density for traditional comparable company analysis. The identified private competitors—Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air—represent the nearest reference universe, though none qualifies as a tight stage or valuation-tier match. No public comparables exist in the narrow Drones & Autonomous category, eliminating public market triangulation.

The peer-median method is inapplicable here. A meaningful peer cluster requires a minimum of three same-stage or adjacent-stage companies with similar valuation characteristics; the available data satisfies neither threshold. Applying an all-sector median across the six private peers would introduce unacceptable noise, as heterogeneity in business models, capital intensity, and commercialization timelines within autonomous systems is substantial.

This analysis cannot support a specific valuation range without additional data on Terra Drone's financials, revenue, growth trajectory, and capital structure. Prospective valuation work would require either (1) direct financials enabling DCF modeling, (2) Tokyo-listed drone or autonomous systems peers that may serve as public anchors, or (3) transaction data from the identified private comparables. The sector's nascent public market presence and limited private exit history constrain analytical leverage materially.
